messages:
emma_support: Customer on Dedicated EU-prod hitting repeated 429s after 03:15 UTC deploy. Reports latency spikes and unexpected billing jump. sample acct: acct-xyz. Can someone triage?
rajesh_repl: Thanks @emma — can you paste the top error payload and any X-* headers?
emma_support: paste: ```HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 1000
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 24
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "reserved pool exhausted for customer acct-xyz"
}
```
olivia_sre: I'm seeing a matching spike in ingress QPS on the EU dedicated gateway at 03:14-03:18. Bucket refill config set to 1000 QPS, 60s window. Thundering: many short-lived bursts from the customer's job queue.
mike_platform: Are they on reserved pool RP-EU-3? If so headroom should be 20% spare. Can you confirm reserved pool assignment?
stella_engineering: Confirmed RP-EU-3. We've got a recent change to routing that sharded traffic differently — could reduce effective headroom.
rajesh_repl: Repro steps requested from customer. Emma, can you get them to run a small curl script so we can reproduce? Example: 
```bash
for i in {1..1200}; do
  curl -s -D - -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":16}' &
  sleep 0.02
done
```
emma_support: Sent repro script. Customer ran it and got ~22% 429s, and invoices show token billing continues for accepted requests but not for 429s. They also saw auth failures intermittently (401) early in the window.
billing-bot: Note: Billing shows a 3x token spike for acct-xyz between 03:10-03:20 UTC; with reserved pool consumption at 98%. Default billing policy applied.
olivia_sre: 401s likely from short-lived API key rotation on client's side hitting our auth endpoint; those 401 retries amplified QPS. Need logs from auth service for that timeframe.
mike_platform: Quick mitigations: 1) Temporary soft-cap override to increase RP-EU-3 capacity by +15% for this account 2) Enable per-customer smoothing (burst window 250ms) 3) Add fallback routing to second dedicated pool in other region if latency allows. Which is easiest?
stella_engineering: We can apply soft-cap override from platform console; takes ~5min. Smoothing change requires config deploy but can be hot-rolled per-customer policy. Fallback routing needs policy update and risk check.
rajesh_repl: For repro, we reproduced locally by running the script against a staging dedicated pool and saw same pattern. Root cause looks like simultaneous job restarts + key rotation -> auth retries -> saturate token bucket window.
emma_support: Customer wants immediate relief and wants billing credit for duplicates caused by retries.
mike_platform: I'll spin up soft-cap override for acct-xyz on RP-EU-3 now and tag on-call for auth logs.
deploy-bot: started playbook: increase-reserved-capacity acct-xyz RP-EU-3 +15% (started) — run id 9876
olivia_sre: I'll pull auth service logs 03:00-03:30 and share snippets. Expect >4000 auth attempts/second at 03:14.
stella_engineering: After override we should monitor x-rate-limit-remaining header and response times. Plan to roll smoothing config in 30min if spike persists.
emma_support: I'll update customer: we're applying capacity bump and investigating auth rotation. Also asking for their retry/backoff settings. :+1:
rajesh_repl: Follow-up checklist for postmortem: - client retry policy and key rotation behavior - reserved pool sizing vs observed burst pattern - per-customer burst smoothing default - billing adjustments for retry-induced tokens - consider circuit-breaker on auth failures
olivia_sre: Added SLO hit marker for RP-EU-3 at 03:14 in incident tracking.
mike_platform: If customer accepts fallback, we can route low-priority requests to fallback pool until they fix retries. Need customer opt-in.
emma_support: Customer opted for temporary capacity bump and will delay their cron restarts. Closing loop once logs confirm auth fix. :white_check_mark:
